title: 昴 (Subaru — The Pleiades)
description:
One of the most iconic Japanese songs of the postwar era, 昴 (1980) was written and composed by 谷村新司 (Tanimura Shinji) of the group アリス (Alice). The song takes its title from 昴 (Subaru), the Japanese name for the Pleiades star cluster, and uses the night sky as a metaphor for human destiny and the individual's determination to forge their own path. Tanimura has said he wrote the final line 「さらば昴よ」(Farewell, Pleiades) first, then built the song around it. The song has become a cultural touchstone in Japan and was famously loved by Chinese audiences as well.

For learners: This is poetic, literary Japanese at N3 level with some classical or elevated vocabulary. Key words and phrases: 哀しくて (feeling sad), 荒野 (wilderness/wasteland), 宿命 (fate/destiny), 砕け散る (to shatter and scatter), 密やかに (quietly/secretly), 照せ (imperative of 照らす — to illuminate), 蒼白き (pale/ashen — literary adjective form), 凩 (kogarashi — cold wintry wind; a challenging kanji), さんざめく (to glitter and murmur), 鮮やかに (vividly), 心の命ずるままに (as one's heart commands). The repeated phrase 「我は行く」(I shall go) gives the song a classical, resolute tone.
